task: fresh-context stratified capability-vs-style and ecosystem audit

items.proposed_content: A monotone counting function and its generalized inverse carry the same leading asymptotic once the logarithmic factor is shown stable under the change of variables. The proof separates an exact inverse relation at jump points from a squeeze argument between jumps.
Counting information transfers to local density by finite differences and to ordered locations by generalized inversion; binning then converts local counts into weighted-sum estimates.
A difficult global analytic burden is replaced by a tunable finite-tail decomposition whose spectral separation supplies decay.

The source develops canonical products in three layers: prescribed zeros are made into a convergent entire product, finite-order growth forces any remaining zero-free factor to be the exponential of a bounded-degree polynomial, and the same architecture is specialized to reciprocal Gamma and completed zeta, where logarithmic differentiation turns products into sums over their zeros.

Three routes reach the completed zeta symmetry by exposing different structure: contour deformation turns the pole lattice of 1/(e^z-1) into zeta values, Fourier expansion turns the periodic fractional-part error into the reflected Dirichlet series, and theta self-reciprocity turns a split Mellin integral into an expression invariant under s mapped to 1-s.

Partial summation turns coefficient partial sums into convergence and regularity control for a Dirichlet series, uniqueness recovers coefficients from the behavior of its sum-function toward the right, and Perron's kernel reverses the encoding more sharply by extracting a cutoff partial sum from a vertical integral; an alternative contour estimate obtains this extraction without a global order estimate for the sum-function.

Finite-domain maximum control is transported to infinite strips by analytic multipliers that suppress uncontrolled ends or normalize unequal boundary data; after applying a maximum principle, the multiplier is removed by a parameter or height limit to obtain stripwise and asymptotic interpolation.

The source assigns different inversion jobs to different transforms: vertical Mellin/Perron integrals recover data organized by multiplicative scale, Fourier and Poisson inversion expose periodic structure and sign information, and a compactly supported triangular Fourier multiplier turns local boundary analyticity into the smoothed identity needed for a Tauberian limit.

Positivity enters twice before the prime number theorem: Euler-product coefficients support boundary nonvanishing and a positive-coefficient singularity obstruction, while the nonnegative monotone prime-counting transform satisfies the Tauberian hypotheses that convert the remaining simple pole at one into asymptotic growth.

Completion packages zeta's pole and Gamma factor into an entire symmetric function; Stirling-scale growth then places that function in the order-one canonical-product theory, and the resulting zero set can also be counted by the argument principle, whose global asymptotic yields local density and summability information.

Real-part bounds are converted into coefficient and derivative estimates, then applied to the analytic logarithm of an entire function after the zeros inside a circle are divided out; the resulting logarithmic-derivative bound is the analytic estimate used in the Hadamard factorization argument.
